0.0.n: A conversational opener here, rather than an answer to a question.

0.2.n: Part of ということで, a common phrase for moving on to the next topic.

0.3.n: こと means a matter or situation and forms part of the transition ということで.

0.4.n: で completes ということで, linking the situation to what follows.

0.5.n: ね gives the transition a friendly, conversational tone.

0.7.n: 今 refers to the speaker's very recent arrival here.

0.8.n: 帰る becomes 帰って, adds くる for returning here, then uses て to connect to what follows.

1.0.n: 今 modifies 時間 through の to describe the current time.

1.1.n: の links 今 to 時間, making the phrase mean the current time.

1.2.n: 時間 refers to the clock time here, not a duration.

1.3.n: が marks the current time as what is being identified.

1.4.n: 時 after a number indicates a clock hour; the phrase itself does not specify morning or evening.

1.5.n: な is the linking form used after a noun before explanatory んです.

1.6.n: ん is shortened の and presents the time as background information.

1.7.n: です makes the explanation polite.

1.8.n: けど gently connects to the next thought here, rather than expressing a strong contrast.

2.0.n: This is the first part of the hesitation filler えっと, split across two tokens.

2.1.n: This completes えっと; it is not the usual particle と here.

2.2.n: ね makes the hesitation sound conversational and directed toward the listener.

2.4.n: 今 combines with から to mark when the planned activities begin.

2.5.n: から marks the starting point in time.

2.6.n: 編集する becomes 編集して, connecting editing to the next planned activity.

3.0.n: The destination particle に or へ is omitted in this casual phrase.

3.1.n: 行って is the て-form of 行く, continuing the list of planned actions.

4.0.n: At the start of a phrase, で casually links back to the previous thought.

4.2.n: 明日 gives the day when the speaker also has work.

4.3.n: も marks tomorrow as another day with work.

4.4.n: お adds a polite or gentle tone to 仕事, even when referring to one's own work.

4.5.n: で is the connecting form of だ here, linking the statement about work to the next explanation.

5.0.n: 一応 lightly qualifies the shift information, presenting it as the current arrangement.

5.1.n: 中番 names a work shift between the early and late shifts.

5.2.n: の links the shift type to お仕事.

5.3.n: お仕事 is a softer, more polite version of 仕事.

5.4.n: の links お仕事 to 日, describing a day scheduled for work.

5.5.n: 日 is the main noun in the phrase describing a middle-shift workday.

5.6.n: な links the noun 日 to the reason-giving expression ので.

5.7.n: ので gives the reason for the speaker's plans that follow.

6.0.n: 今日 sets the day for the speaker's self-care plans.

6.1.n: は marks today as the topic, while ね adds a friendly conversational touch.

6.3.n: ちゃんと emphasizes doing the care thoroughly rather than skipping or rushing it.

6.4.n: 自分 refers to the speaker here.

6.5.n: の links 自分 to ケア, identifying care of the speaker themself.

6.6.n: ケア is borrowed from English and refers to looking after oneself here.

6.8.n: 毎日 modifies ケア through の to describe a daily routine.

6.9.n: の turns 毎日 into a description of the care.

6.10.n: The speaker restates the care as their everyday routine.

6.11.n: を marks ケア as what the speaker will do.

6.12.n: Repeating ちゃんと reinforces the intention to take care of the routine thoroughly.

6.13.n: して is the て-form of する and combines with から to put this action first.

6.14.n: After a verb's て-form, から means the next action happens once this one is completed.

7.0.n: まあ softens the plan and gives it a casual, reflective tone.

7.1.n: 時 marks a clock hour; the bedtime context suggests one in the morning.

7.2.n: くらい makes the stated time approximate.

7.3.n: まで combines with に to set a deadline rather than a duration.

7.4.n: に completes までに, marking when the action should happen at the latest.

7.5.n: は emphasizes the deadline, suggesting the speaker wants to be asleep by then at least.

7.6.n: 寝よう is the intention form of 寝る, expressing what the speaker is considering doing.

7.7.n: か combines with な to express gentle uncertainty about the speaker's own plan.

7.8.n: な completes かな, making the intention sound tentative rather than firmly decided.

7.9.n: と marks the preceding tentative plan as the content of the speaker's thought.

7.10.n: 思います is the polite form of 思う and frames the bedtime plan as a personal intention.

0.lit: All right, with that being the case, you know, just now having come back,
0.tip: 帰ってきて connects returning home to the next statement; this ending does not finish the sentence.

1.lit: The time of now is eight o'clock, and,
1.tip: なんですけど provides background politely and leads into more speech, without necessarily meaning but.

2.lit: Um, you know, from now, editing,
2.tip: 今から signals starting now, while 編集して begins a connected list of plans.

3.tip: Casual speech often drops the destination particle, so ジム行って means ジムに行って.

4.lit: And, tomorrow too is work, and,
4.tip: The first で links thoughts; the last で connects a statement ending in a noun.

5.lit: As things stand, because it is a day of middle-shift work,
5.tip: After a noun, なので gives a reason: because it is that kind of day.

6.lit: Today, you know, properly, care of myself, everyday care, after doing it properly,
6.tip: してから establishes the order: finish the self-care first, then do what follows.

7.lit: Well, by around one o'clock at least, I think, perhaps I'll go to sleep.
7.tip: 寝ようかなと思います expresses a tentative personal plan, softer than a definite promise to sleep.
